$comment: A machine-readable orientation to this repository, written for a language model reading it cold. Prose lives in README.md and PRODUCT.md; this file is the map. Keep it accurate or delete it — a stale map is worse than none.

project.name: Wavr
project.one_line: An open, local-first spatial intelligence platform: it turns local network and sensor observations into an explainable model of a physical Space.
project.problem: Understanding what is happening in a physical Space -- who is present, where, and how sure anyone can be about it -- normally means renting that understanding from somebody else's cloud. Wavr does the same sensing on hardware the owner controls, keeps the data there, and shows its reasoning.
project.maturity: early; used by one person on one household's devices
project.version_source_of_truth: VERSION at the repository root; backend/tests/test_the_version_is_one_number.py fails the build when any surface disagrees.
project.$positioning_note: A Space is a home, an office, a shop -- the model is not home-specific, and identity is contextual (a person, a role, a device function) rather than a label stamped on a MAC address. See docs/adr/0009 and docs/VOCABULARY.md.
project.$license_note: Commercial use is permitted under the AGPL's own terms. There is no separate commercial licence on offer: designing one is a deliberate future decision, and advertising it before the terms exist would be a promise nobody could honour.
project.$visibility_note: Published 2026-09-09. The unsanitized development history stayed behind in a separate private archive; this repository's history is the sanitized one. scripts/publication_gate.py still runs and still lists what a visibility change would make false.

core_idea.fusion_rule: Confidence is the strength of the best PRESENT evidence -- trust weight x the source's own confidence x freshness decay -- reduced by fresh, trusted evidence of ABSENCE.
core_idea.why_not_averaging: Averaging lets several weak, agreeing sources manufacture certainty, and it lets a disagreement be smoothed into a number nobody can account for. Taking the strongest single piece of positive evidence, and letting a trusted negative pull against it, keeps both the confidence and the doubt attributable to a named source.
core_idea.explainability: Every source's own reading is surfaced next to the fused number rather than silently arbitrated. The user can always ask why.
core_idea.$fusion_detail: Two halves. (1) The strongest single present reading sets the strength, so a confident answer always has one nameable reason behind it. (2) A source that can genuinely prove absence, is still fresh, and reports empty enters the denominator at its own aged trust -- it lowers certainty rather than being averaged away. Silence is NOT contradiction, and neither is a negative from a source that cannot prove absence: a still person vanishes from radar, so a fresh mmWave 'empty' is a dropout, not an empty room. Only fusion.TRUSTED_ABSENCE_MODALITIES qualify. There is no Bayesian posterior here and the code does not pretend otherwise.

invariants.$comment: These are enforced in code and covered by tests. A change that breaks one is a product decision, not a refactor.
invariants.loopback_only_by_default: The base install never opens a LAN socket. Peer check + Host allowlist + CSRF header.
invariants.cameras_boot_off: Frames live in RAM only, are never written to disk, and never leave the machine.
invariants.derived_state_only: Raw sensing is never persisted. What IS persisted is derived state and the configuration the product needs to run -- see storage_layers below.
invariants.egress_is_opt_in: Every path off the machine — LAN multi-device, MQTT, the MCP control tool, the narrator, the diagnostics report — is default-OFF and individually switched on. The receiving end of the diagnostics path is in infra/wavr-diag-worker/, in this repository, so what it does with a report is readable rather than promised.
invariants.no_telemetry: No analytics SDK, no crash reporter, no account, and nothing is sent anywhere by default. The dashboard and the companion make zero external requests. The one path that CAN leave is the diagnostics connector: default-OFF, switched on by hand, MAC-redacted before it is sent and again on arrival. Off is not the same as absent, and this says which one it is.
invariants.credentials_never_echoed: Tokens and keys are never logged, returned, or printed.

surfaces.name: backend
surfaces.what: The fusion engine and the HTTP/WS API. FastAPI on Python 3.11.
surfaces.notes: No mandatory heavy dependencies. torch/cv2, pyserial, paho, bleak, cryptography and genai are lazy optional extras.

surfaces.name: frontend
surfaces.what: The dashboard. Vanilla JS, no bundler: a static index.html shell plus classic scripts in frontend/js/ loaded in a pinned order.
surfaces.notes: Top-level declarations cross <script> boundaries but hoisting does not, so the order in index.html is load-bearing. three.js is vendored same-origin. Opened off localhost it self-switches to a simulator and says so on screen.

surfaces.name: desktop
surfaces.what: Tauri v2 shell (Rust) that hosts the dashboard and supervises a PyInstaller onefile sidecar of the backend.
surfaces.notes: The machine running it is the 'central'. The sidecar is confined to a Windows Job Object so a killed shell cannot leave an orphan Core holding the port.

surfaces.name: mobile
surfaces.what: Android companion, Capacitor shell plus native Kotlin plugins. Pairs to a central over certificate-pinned TLS.
surfaces.notes: Discovery uses Android's NsdManager rather than an in-process mDNS browse, because a phone VPN routes multicast into its tunnel and an in-app browse never reaches the LAN. Pairing sends a salted hash of ANDROID_ID so re-pairing retires this device's earlier credentials instead of stacking another live key. `mobile/www/` is BUILD OUTPUT, produced from `frontend/` by `mobile/scripts/sync-frontend.mjs`; the vendored `mobile/vendor/jsqr.js` reads the pairing QR and is phone-only source.

surfaces.name: core-launcher
surfaces.what: Android home-launcher app that turns a dedicated phone into an always-on hub: ambient panel, mDNS advertisement, kiosk.
surfaces.notes: Advertises `_wavr._tcp` on the LAN only while its own kiosk page load succeeds, so the network is never invited to a Core that is not serving. Ran on a physical handset on 2026-09-08.

surfaces.name: firmware
surfaces.what: ESP32 sensor nodes: MQTT, OTA, enrolment and revocation.

sensing_modalities.$comment: `status` is the field that stops this list from reading as six equivalent capabilities. Two of them have never been run against the hardware they name, and one is not a Wavr source at all.

sensing_modalities.name: network
sensing_modalities.how: ARP, DHCP, mDNS, SSDP, NetBIOS, SNMP — device presence inferred from the LAN itself

sensing_modalities.name: bluetooth
sensing_modalities.how: BLE proximity with RSSI and confidence decay

sensing_modalities.name: camera
sensing_modalities.how: RTSP/ONVIF plus person detection; frames stay in RAM

sensing_modalities.name: mmwave
sensing_modalities.status: code and mock tests; ZERO validation on real hardware

sensing_modalities.name: wifi_csi
sensing_modalities.how: channel-state sensing, consumed from an EXTERNAL service over its WebSocket -- there is no Wavr CSI source
sensing_modalities.hardware: a supported radio, plus the external service that reads it
sensing_modalities.status: seam only, not a shipped source

sensing_modalities.name: uwb
sensing_modalities.status: code and mock tests; ZERO validation on real hardware

vocabulary.$comment: Words this project uses on purpose. docs/VOCABULARY.md is the authority; several are admin-only and must never appear in an end-user screen.
vocabulary.Space: The place being watched — a home, an office, a shop. Has people and rooms.
vocabulary.Core: The machine that thinks: runs fusion and holds the database. ADMIN WORD — never shown to a household user.
vocabulary.Node: A sensor board that reports to a Core. ADMIN WORD — never shown to a household user.
vocabulary.Client: A device that only views. A phone, a tablet, a browser.
vocabulary.central: A credential role meaning 'may administer'. Distinct from being a Core, which is a device function.
vocabulary.RoomState: The one answer per room: occupied, how sure, and why.

how_to_run.backend_dev: cd backend && pip install -e ".[dev]" && cd .. && python -m wavr.serve
how_to_run.test_notes: Every hardware path is mock-tested, so the whole suite runs with no devices attached. Browser tests use Playwright. The cross-language checks that compare the Core against the companion read `mobile/` from this repository and FAIL rather than skip if it is missing — a skipped guarantee reports coverage the run does not have.
how_to_run.multi_device: Off by default. Set WAVR_MULTIDEVICE=1 or turn it on in Settings; it changes what the process is exposed to, so it is a deliberate, separate step.
how_to_run.mcp: python -m wavr.mcp_serve over stdio, or the HTTP transport. Read-only by default; Home Assistant control is a separate opt-in, gated tool.
how_to_run.mobile:
node mobile/scripts/sync-frontend.mjs   # packages frontend/ into mobile/www/
node --test mobile/test/*.test.js       # companion unit tests, no npm needed
cd mobile && npx cap sync android && (cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug)

conventions.code_language: English — code, comments, commit messages and documentation, always.
conventions.tests_are_named_as_sentences: A test file is called what it guarantees, e.g. test_the_screen_never_invents_a_house.py, and its docstring says what failure it exists to prevent.
conventions.a_guarantee_needs_a_producer: The dominant defect class in this repository is a check that works with nothing on the other side producing what it checks. When adding a guarantee, verify the producing half exists and is called.
conventions.measure_dont_guess: Vague symptoms ('it feels slow', 'it doesn't find it') have specific causes. A wrong hypothesis costs more than the measurement would have.
conventions.no_machine_details: This repository never describes the maintainer's personal hardware — model, CPU, GPU, RAM, monitor count or exact OS. The allowed form is 'tested on one machine'.

where_to_look.$agent_contract_note: Canonical and model-neutral. CLAUDE.md is a thin adapter over it and loses to it on any disagreement.

known_gaps: The Android Core's EMBEDDED-engine build (ADR-0010) is specified and not exercised. What was physically tested on 2026-09-08 is a different topology: the core-launcher app running as the device's home screen, with the ordinary Python backend beside it in a Debian container. That hub serves the current dashboard over the LAN and restarts unattended after a reboot; the embedded build remains untested.

Radar (mmWave) and UWB have code paths and mock tests and ZERO validation on real hardware -- not 'little time', none. Wi-Fi CSI is a seam that consumes an external service, not a source this project ships.

The companion's screens are routed through the dashboard's translator and carry Portuguese, but nothing has yet driven them in Portuguese on a real handset — the language was verified by the catalogue guards and by reading, not by using the app in it.
The website exists in `site/` and is deliberately not deployed.

Several files are large enough to be real architectural debt — `backend/wavr/app.py`, `desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`, the Core launcher's MainActivity. Recorded rather than split, because splitting to lower a line count is a refactor looking for a reason.

not_true_of_this_project.$comment: Stated explicitly because a reader — human or model — may otherwise assume the usual.
not_true_of_this_project.no_users_or_customers: There are no users beyond the maintainer, no customers, no paying installations, and no production deployment.
not_true_of_this_project.no_uptime_or_scale_claims: No availability, install-count or scale figure in this repository is a measurement of real-world usage.
not_true_of_this_project.not_a_medical_device: Vitals-adjacent sensing is presence and motion only. It diagnoses nothing and must never be described as health monitoring (ADR-0003).

storage_layers.$comment: An earlier version of this file said only occupancy, confidence and timestamps are stored. That was materially wrong -- the database holds over thirty tables -- and 'a stale map is worse than none' applies to this file first.
storage_layers.never_persisted: Camera frames, pose keypoints, raw radar frames, audio. Consumed in memory and dropped. Enforced by backend/tests/test_a_frame_never_reaches_the_disk.py.
storage_layers.live_only: Per-person x/y targets and vitals. They travel over the live WebSocket and are never written to SQLite or published to MQTT: a movement history on disk is a liability this product refuses by design.
storage_layers.derived_and_historical: Per-room occupancy, confidence, the per-source evidence behind it, and the occupancy log with its retention window. This is the product's output and it is meant to be queryable.
storage_layers.operational: Everything that makes an install work and stay secure: paired devices and their hashed credentials, people and roles, consent tiers, rooms and the house map, cameras and their masked URLs, enrolled nodes, connectors, calibration, settings, discovery inbox, routines. Not sensing data, but not nothing either -- an owner erasing a Space is erasing this too.
